findings.area: documentation / ADR evidence (task 4.8 / F2 native byte-identity correction)
findings.summary: RESOLVED: ADR-015, docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md, docs/implementation-readiness.md, and the attempt-1 worker report now correctly state the pinned musl host's native libSkiaSharp.so is byte-identical to the NuGet 3.119.4 linux-musl-x64 asset and differs from the linux-x64 asset the plugin previously bundled, with the matching-RID qualification.
findings.detail: Verified the corrected wording in all four required surfaces. docs/decisions.md:1885-1896 states the host native is 18,453,464 B / SHA-256 59039b25..., byte-identical to the NuGet SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux 3.119.4 runtimes/linux-musl-x64/native/ asset (and to the file inside the pinned Jellyfin distribution), differing from the runtimes/linux-x64/native/ asset (11,170,296 B / 66c856ea...) the glibc spike host matched, and explicitly says 'Native byte-identity therefore holds for the matching RID, not across RIDs.' docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md:83-95 adds the F2 correction with the same RID qualification; docs/implementation-readiness.md:176-182 states byte-identity holds for the matching RID, the glibc spike matched linux-x64, and the pinned musl host's native is byte-identical to the linux-musl-x64 asset; docs/implementation/7.8/worker-report.json known_limitations[3] carries the same corrected statement. Independently re-verified against the actual artifacts: sha256sum of /tmp/jf/jellyfin/libSkiaSharp.so = 59039b2548e3a3f563fa247f582c62d280c2015df78316fcab62e383d7ae9d4f (18,453,464 B); the NuGet linux-musl-x64 asset = the same hash/size; the NuGet linux-x64 asset = 66c856eaf1a47a00b23204c30c6ee407987bf5086ecc0a1a6b4fd67526b0cd02 (11,170,296 B); extracting jellyfin/libSkiaSharp.so from /tmp/jf/jellyfin.tar.gz also yields 59039b25.../18,453,464 B. The pinned host's own jellyfin.deps.json runtimeTarget is '.NETCoreApp,Version=v10.0/linux-musl-x64', confirming the host is musl. The managed SkiaSharp.dll is aaaaa18c... on both the host and NuGet 3.119.4 lib/net10.0, so the managed byte-identity claim is host-independent and unchanged. No remaining 'not the NuGet' framing exists in any current-state or decision document.
evidence: docs/decisions.md:1885-1896 (ADR-015 F2 correction with matching-RID qualification)
findings.recommended_action: None. Correction is accurate and verified; no further action required.
